description: Fig. 3 is a two-panel line-drawing schematic (no micrographs, curves or data plots) that defines the multiaxial forging (MAF) specimen geometry and the sampling plan for the studied Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel. Panel (a) is a 3-D isometric block of the MAFed workpiece, dimensioned 30 mm along the bottom edge, with vertical dimensions marked 20 and 10 on the left and depth dimensions 20 and 10 along the top-left diagonal edge; a shaded central plate labelled "Analysed area for XRD, EBSD" carries a large blue arrow marking the pressing direction. Two grey ellipses on the right-hand face mark the locations from which test specimens were extracted, and blue arrows connect those locations to panel (b). Panel (b) contains two drawings: a miniature round tensile specimen with gauge length 16 mm, overall length 26.5 mm and fillet radius R1, plus a circular cross-section giving Ø7.2 for the shoulder and Ø4 for the gauge; beneath it an orthogonal arrow triad labels the "Constrained direction", "Flow direction" and "Pressing direction". The caption states all dimensions are in mm. Together the panels show which volume was probed by XRD/EBSD and where the tensile specimens were cut, fixing the strain path and testing geometry of the study.

observations.observation: The figure consists of two line-drawing schematics only; there are no micrographs, spectra, maps or data curves in either panel.
Panel (a) shows a rectangular 3-D block of the MAF sample with the dimension '30' marked along its bottom edge.
Panel (a) marks vertical dimensions of 20 and 10 on the left-hand side of the block and depth dimensions of 20 and 10 along the upper-left edge.
Panel (a) contains a shaded mid-height plate annotated 'Analysed area for XRD, EBSD', indicating the volume probed by diffraction and EBSD.
A large blue arrow at the centre of panel (a) marks the pressing direction of the forging operation.
Two grey ellipses on the right-hand face of the block in panel (a) mark the locations from which specimens were cut, and blue arrows connect these locations to the tensile specimen in panel (b).
Panel (b) shows a miniature round tensile specimen with gauge length 16 mm, total length 26.5 mm and shoulder fillet radius R1.
The circular cross-section inset in panel (b) is annotated Ø7.2 for the outer/shoulder diameter and Ø4 for the gauge diameter.
Panel (b) includes an orthogonal arrow triad labelled 'Constrained direction', 'Flow direction' and 'Pressing direction'.
The caption states that all dimensions in Fig. 3 are in mm.
The caption states that panel (a) shows the location of samples taken for various tests/characterisations and panel (b) the tensile sample geometry.
The citing text states that XRD and EBSD characterisation was performed at the location shown in Fig. 3(a), with equivalent strains of 0, 0.47, 1.4 and 2.34 imposed at four MAF levels.

The citing text states that miniature round tensile samples at MAF-0, MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5 were cut from the located area shown in Fig. 3(a) and tested at a strain rate of 1×10⁻³ s⁻¹ at room temperature.
The citing text states the XRD measurements used Co-Kα radiation, 2θ from 40°–120°, scan speed 2° per minute and step size 0.02°.
